His Kura inscription dates to 495–500 and the Sanjeli copper plate to 502–503; Kausambi was probably sacked by his Alkhons in 497–500. The Eran boar inscription is dated to the first year of his reign, placed between 510 and 513. Prakashadharma of Malwa defeats him in 515.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, infobox, Defeats, Sack of Kausambi and Punjab inscription

events.title: Bhanugupta’s Eran inscription
events.descr: An inscription at Eran records that Bhanugupta took part in a battle in 510 CE (Fleet’s 1888 reading); a 1981 translation reads it as a battle against the “Maittras”. The Toramana page says Toramana may have been defeated by Bhanugupta in 510, per this inscription; the new reading removes that link.

sources.sourceLocation: Initial translation (J.F Fleet 1888) and New translation (1981)

events.title: Mihirakula rules the Alchon Huns
events.descr: He rules from 515; the Chinese monk Song Yun meets him around 520. His campaign is reversed at Sondani, and Xuanzang says the Gupta king Narasimhagupta Baladitya defeated and captured him.

events.title: Yashodharman defeats Mihirakula at Sondani
events.descr: Yashodharman, and possibly the Gupta emperor Narasimhagupta, defeat a Huna army under Mihirakula and drive the Huns out of India. Yashodharman’s Mandsaur stone inscription is dated 532 AD.

sources.sourceLocation: lead and Mandsaur Pillar inscriptions of Yashodharman

source.sourceLocation: lead ('between 525 and 532 CE, likely by 530 CE')

events.title: Reign of Vima Kadphises
events.descr: Kushan emperor from approximately 113 to 127 CE. The same page also gives 90–100 CE (navbox) and AD 100–127 (a quoted source).

events.title: Vasudeva I, the last great Kushan
events.descr: The last of the “Great Kushans”; his reign extended from at least 191 to 232 CE. He sent tribute to China in 229.

sources.sourceLocation: short description, infobox, lead, Contacts with China and Sassanid invasion in the northwest

events.title: Shelun takes the title khagan
events.descr: Yujiulü Shelun, crowned 11 March 402, rules the Rouran until 410. He is the first major leader of the steppes to take the title khagan.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, infobox, Reign and Personality and achievements

events.title: Peroz I’s wars with the Hephthalites
events.descr: Peroz attacks the Hephthalites in 474 and is ambushed and captured near the border of Gurgan; ransomed, he is defeated and captured again in a second campaign in the late 470s or early 480s, and sends his son Kavad to the Hephthalite court as a hostage in 482. In 484, charging at Akhshunwar’s forces, he and his army fall into a trench and are killed.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, infobox, First and second war with the Hephthalites, Third war with the Hephthalites and death

events.title: Battle of the Utus
events.descr: A Hunnic victory over the Eastern Roman field armies; Arnegisclus is killed and Marcianople falls. Peace comes with a treaty in the fall of 447 or in 448: 6,000 lbs of gold up front and 2,100 lbs a year.

events.title: Attila invades Italy
events.descr: Attila returns in 452 to renew his claim to Honoria, razes Aquileia and halts at the River Po. Pope Leo I and two envoys meet him at the Mincio near Mantua and obtain his promise to withdraw; Italy had suffered famine in 451, and an East Roman force had crossed the Danube. He dies in the early months of 453.

sources.sourceLocation: lead and Invasion of Italy and death

events.title: Battle of Thapsus
events.descr: Caesar defeats the Optimates under Metellus Scipio, with Juba I of Numidia, on 6 April 46 BC (the pre-reform Roman calendar; 7 February by the Julian). Cato commits suicide on news of the defeat, and Juba has a slave kill him after a duel with Petreius. Caesar returns to Rome on 25 July.

events.title: Persia conquers Egypt
events.descr: The Persian invasion begins in 617 or 618; Alexandria is betrayed to the Persians in June 619 (Khuzistan Chronicle), and by 621 the province is securely in Persian hands. Egypt stays Persian for 10 years: in the summer of 629 the Persian troops begin to leave.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, infobox, Fall of Egypt and Aftermath

events.title: Marius defeats the Teutons at Aquae Sextiae
events.descr: At Aquae Sextiae (Aix-en-Provence) the Romans under Gaius Marius defeat the Teutons and Ambrones.

events.title: Battle of Vercellae
events.descr: On 30 July 101 BC, near Vercellae in Cisalpine Gaul, Marius and Catulus defeat a Celtic-Germanic confederation under the Cimbric king Boiorix, ending the Cimbrian War.

events.title: Vercingetorix executed
events.descr: Forced to surrender at Alesia in September 52 BC, Vercingetorix is imprisoned in Rome for six years and executed after Caesar’s triumph in 46 BC.

events.title: Germanicus campaigns in Germania
events.descr: Between 14 and 16 Germanicus leads punitive operations against the Germanic tribes, defeating Arminius twice (according to Tacitus), first at Idistaviso. Roman troops recover one of the three lost legionary eagles in 15 and a second in 16. Germanicus dies in Antioch on 10 October 19; Arminius, seeking to become a king, is murdered by opponents in his own tribe in 21.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, infobox and Roman retribution and death

events.title: Battle of Abritus: the Goths kill Decius
events.descr: In the summer of 251 (June, July or August), near Abritus (modern Razgrad) in Moesia Inferior, Goths under Cniva defeat the Roman army; the emperors Decius and his son Herennius Etruscus are both killed.

events.title: The Goths reach the Danube
events.descr: In the summer of 376 a massive number of Goths arrive on the Danube; the Thervings are probably allowed to cross at or near Durostorum. The Gothic War that follows lasts until 382.

events.title: Hengist and Horsa (traditional date)
events.descr: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records that in 449 Vortigern invited Hengist and Horsa to Britain to help fight the Picts; the History of the Britons gives 447. Bede names them as the first chieftains of the Angles, Saxons and Jutes in England.

sources.sourceLocation: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, History of the Britons and Ecclesiastical History

events.title: Battle of Badon
events.descr: A Brittonic victory whose date is unknown. Scholars have proposed 493, 501 and 516; McCarthy and Ó Cróinín revise it to February 482 and Breeze (2020) to 493. Bede’s chronology implies 493–500. Gildas’s account was written c. 543–547.

events.title: The Rule of the Dukes
events.descr: An interregnum in the Lombard kingdom (574/5–584/5): after King Cleph dies, the dukes rule without a king for ten years (Paul the Deacon) or twelve (the Origo Gentis Langobardorum). After invading Frankish Provence in 584/5 they elect Cleph’s son Authari king.

events.title: Tikal founds Dos Pilas
events.descr: The Tikal king Kʼinich Muwaan Jol II installs his four-year-old son Bʼalaj Chan Kʼawiil as ruler of Dos Pilas, an offshoot of the Tikal dynasty.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, infobox and 629: Aligned to Tikal

events.title: Yuknoom Chʼeen II rules Calakmul
events.descr: He accedes on 1 May 636; his successor takes the throne in 686.

events.title: Dos Pilas defects to Calakmul
events.descr: Dos Pilas breaks away from Tikal and becomes a vassal of Calakmul; Yuknoom Chʼeen II reinstates Bʼalaj Chan Kʼawiil on its throne as his vassal. (The Yuknoom Chʼeen II page dates his expulsion to 650.)

events.title: Bhadravarman I of Champa
events.descr: King of Champa from 380 to 413 and author of several Sanskrit inscriptions; he builds temples and palaces at Mỹ Sơn and Trà Kiệu. He campaigns north in 399 and fights the Chinese governor from 405 to 413.

events.title: Bhrikuti marries Songtsen Gampo
events.descr: A Nepalese princess and the Tibetan king’s first queen, though her historicity is not certain and the date of the marriage is unknown: presumably about the time Narendradeva fled to Tibet (c. 621), or before 624, while one author gives 632.

events.title: Wu Mingche’s northern campaign
events.descr: In spring 573 Emperor Xuan of Chen attacks Northern Qi; by fall Wu Mingche holds Shouyang, and the land between the Yangtze and the Huai is entirely in Chen hands.

events.title: Northern Zhou captures Wu Mingche
events.descr: After Northern Zhou destroys Northern Qi in 577, the Zhou general Wang Gui captures Wu Mingche and some 30,000 foot soldiers on 20 March 578.

events.title: Himiko rules Yamatai
events.descr: The queen of Yamatai sends her first recorded embassy to the Wei court in 238 (Book of Wei; the Nihon Shoki’s quotation gives 239), another in 243, and envoys to Daifang in 247. She dies in 247 or 248.

events.title: Empress Suiko; Prince Shōtoku regent
events.descr: Suiko ascends the throne after an assassination in 592 (15 January 593 by the Gregorian calendar, 8 December 592 by the lunar) and reigns until her death in 628. Prince Shōtoku is regent from 593 to 621.

events.title: Zhongshan, a non-Zhou state in the north
events.descr: Some sources (Records of the Grand Historian) say Beidi founded and ruled it; others list it only as not Zhou or Han. Wei conquers it in 407, it regains independence in 381, and Zhao annexes it after ten years of war.

source.sourceLocation: History ('in 414 BC ... traditionally considered the founding')

events.title: Qin defeats the last hostile Rong tribe
events.descr: By 400 BC most of the Di and Rong had been eliminated as independent polities.
